title: Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of Marchantia polymorpha
author: Suvi Honkanen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ba28ighw
materials: Sterilisation of dried spores stored in the freezer
Sigma | A9799-1KG | Agar High Gel Strength (Plant Cell Tested)
Sigma | S5939-500EA | Sun Cap Closures 18mm OD (Autoclavable)

steps.title: Collect and Store Spores
steps.instruction: Collect sporangiums from archegoniophores for transformation.

substeps.instruction: Collect 2-7 intact sporangiums with extended stalks into 500 µl sterile dH2O in an Eppendorf tube, or collect without water if sporangiums are burst or intended for drying.
Alternatively, collect archegoniophores with yellow mature sporangiums in a petri dish, placing wet tissue at the thallus end of the stalk to maintain viability.
Allow archegoniophores to mature on the bench (hours/days) or at 4°C (days/weeks) to increase the yield of intact sporangiums.

To store: Dry sporangiums in an open Eppendorf tube with a Sun Cap Closure filter (or micropore tape) for 10 days in an air-tight box with non-saturated silica gel (dry gel at 50°C if needed), then store at -80°C for up to five years.

steps.title: Sterilize Frozen Spores
steps.instruction: Sterilize spores previously stored at -80°C using NaDCC.

substeps.instruction: Thaw frozen spores to room temperature.
Add 500 µl of 0.1% NaDCC (prepared as 450 µl sterile dH2O and 50 µl 1% NaDCC).
Resuspend spores by vortexing and pressing clumps against the tube side with a pipette tip; invert the tube to sterilize the lid.
Let stand for at least 5 minutes.
Centrifuge for 1.5 minutes at 13,000 rpm.
Remove some of the sterilization solution without removing all of it to avoid spore loss.
Wash spores off the tube sides with 500 µl sterile dH2O and add the suspension to liquid culture.

steps.title: Sterilize Fresh Sporangiums
steps.instruction: Sterilize intact sporangiums for immediate use.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl of 1% NaDCC sterilization solution to an Eppendorf tube containing 500 µl H2O and sporangiums (final concentration 0.5% NaDCC).
Gently invert the tube (do not vortex).
Remove the solution after a few minutes (do not exceed a few minutes or germination will be reduced).
Rinse three times with 1 ml dH2O.
Optional: Store intact sporangia in the 3rd 1 ml rinse in the fridge for up to a couple of months.
Add 600 µl water and break the sporangiums to release spores, avoiding the inclusion of sporangium fragments.
Pipette the spore suspension into liquid culture.

steps.title: Set Up Liquid Spore Cultures
steps.instruction: Establish spore growth in Gamborgs medium.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fresh liquid ½ Gamborgs medium containing 150 mg L-glutamine (final concentration 0.03%).
Autoclave the media and let cool.
Set up 25 ml cultures in sterile 250 ml Erlenmeyer flasks (covered with two layers of foil before autoclaving) or 6 ml cultures in sterile 6-well plates (sealed with micropore tape).
Inoculate with spores equivalent to ~1 sterilized sporangium per flask or 0.5-1 sporangium per well.
Grow for 6-7 days at 21-23°C under constant light (1500-2000 lux / 80-100 µM), without shaking.

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium Culture
steps.instruction: Prepare and induce Agrobacterium carrying the desired vector.

substeps.instruction: Streak Agrobacterium (e.g., strain GV3101 with Rif and Gent resistance) on LB containing appropriate antibiotics: 100 µg/ml spec for MpGWB/CRISPR vectors (SHp131, pMpGE011, pMpGE010) or 50 µg/ml Kan for pCambia 1300.
Grow for two days at 28°C.
Inoculate a single colony in 5 ml LB medium with appropriate antibiotics and grow for 1-2 days (or overnight) at 28°C on a shaker.
Centrifuge the culture for 15 minutes at 2000g and pour off the supernatant.

Resuspend the pellet by shaking in fresh ½ Gamborgs liquid medium containing 100 µM acetosyringone (1:1000 dilution of 100 mM stock in DMSO). Use 7 ml for 1-day old cultures or 10 ml for 2-day old cultures.
Induce by cultivating for 2 to 6 hours at 28°C and 200 rpm on a shaker. Stop induction immediately if bacterial clumping is observed.

steps.title: Perform Transformation
steps.instruction: Inoculate spore cultures with induced Agrobacterium and co-cultivate.

substeps.instruction: Add induced Agrobacterium to 6- or 7-day old liquid spore cultures: 100-500 µl for a 6 ml plate well or 1 ml for a 25 ml flask.
Ensure acetosyringone is at a final concentration of 100 µM.
Co-cultivate for 1-3 days on a 120 rpm shaker. Keep cultures in the dark (cover with foil) to potentially improve efficiency.

steps.title: Filter and Plate Spores
steps.instruction: Separate spores from bacteria and plate on selection media.

substeps.instruction: Place a 40 µm cell strainer in the opening of a 50 ml Falcon tube.
For 6-well plates: Transfer spores onto the strainer using a sterile plastic Pasteur pipette; rinse the well with dH2O and move the remaining spores to the strainer.
For 25 ml flasks: Slowly pour the culture through the strainer, shaking slightly.
Rinse spores on the filter with at least 50 ml of autoclaved dH2O.

Transfer spores from the filter using a sterile Pasteur pipette onto 1.4% agar plates containing ½ Gamborgs medium with 100 µg/ml Cefotaxime (to kill Agrobacterium) and either 10 µg/ml Hygromycin or 0.5 µM chlorosulfron for selection.
Distribute spores across 3-8 plates per 25 ml flask (or 1-2 plates per 6 ml well), varying the density to allow for the picking of individual transformants.

steps.title: Incubate and Select Transformants
steps.instruction: Grow plates and identify resistant plants.

substeps.instruction: Place plates in a growth chamber at 21-23°C under constant light or a 16h light/8h dark cycle.
Identify antibiotic-resistant transformants after 1-2 weeks.
When transferring transformants to new plates, continue adding cefotaxime to prevent Agrobacterium regrowth. Cefotaxime can be omitted after several weeks.
